items.title: Lorelei and the Laser Eyes review
items.summary: Good puzzles don't make you feel dumb; they make you feel clever when you solve it. The puzzles in Lorelei and the Laser Eyes are…
items.content_html:
Good puzzles don't make you feel dumb; they make you feel clever when you solve it.

The puzzles in Lorelei and the Laser Eyes are not great. They seem like the clumsy puzzles in cheap escape rooms, you need a code for 4 digit lock? Sure! Throw in some random 4 digit number and put it next to the lock so you know it's for that specific locks. But nothing makes sense to me.

Almost all the puzzles in the game are related to years. But the lock or puzzle itself doesn't feel like it's related to years at all. Basically you just know that it's 4 digit so it must be related to years, which is stupid.

None of the puzzles make me yell out in awe. Most of them feel like brain twisters for kids, or for people who has never played any good puzzle games. It's more like pattern matching. 

They feel super repetitive too, like in the quiz club you need to answer so many random questions that's not even related to any puzzle. It feels a waste of time and I had to pause to take a break so many times.

Sure, unlocking one door gives you access to a new area, but nothing seems exciting in this game.

Overall, I don't recommend this game. If you want a better puzzle game and you don't mind a little action element in it, I highly recommend Animal Well and Tunic. The experience of playing them were full of surprises. You keep learning new things and it makes you in awe. I'm not sure if I can go back to shitty puzzle games anymore.

items.title: Unemployment Diary #1
items.summary: Today is my 4th week since getting laid off. I went through a lot. The first week was a mix of relief and anxiety. I…
items.content_html:
Today is my 4th week since getting laid off.

I went through a lot. The first week was a mix of relief and anxiety. I was actually relieved that i don’t have to work on the bullshit ass project anymore. It was a very frustrating project where I had arguments with my stakeholders all the time. I can tell that they were stressed too. I hated my job and almost glad that I got laid off.

However, losing my job also means that I’d risk losing my work visa. I was on my last year of H1B and right before Flow filing a PERM application for my green card. The lawyers were not responsive in the past few weeks of my employment, which should have been a sign for me. I knew something was going to happen.

The second week was hopeful. I was getting lots of interviews and the companies seem great to work at. I started to have hope in working again.

Fastforward to the 4th week, it feels numbing. I lost track of everything and came down with a really bad cold. I don’t know if I want to work again, yet I was not taking the time to chill and enjoy the perfect weather. I was too stressed to do anything.
